title: Common property regime

definition.text: A common property regime is a social arrangement by which a group regulates the upkeep and use of a shared resource, keeping outsiders out.

facts.text: It differs from open access: in a common property system access is not free, so the resource looks private to outsiders and common to insiders.
Such systems arise when users acting alone threaten the resource's total benefit, and usually work locally to prevent overexploitation.
Hardin's tragedy of the commons was criticized for not distinguishing common property from open-access resources.
Members' local knowledge often lets these regimes outperform rules designed by outside experts, and results are best when they also consult governments and experts.
Ostrom found many common-pool resources governed by such community self-management, distinct from private property or state control.

notes: Phrase concept with no page of its own.

title: Governing the Commons

definition.text: Governing the Commons (1990) is Elinor Ostrom's best-known book, showing that communities worldwide have managed shared resources successfully through local rules.

facts.text: It drew on irrigation systems in Spain and the Philippines, mountain villages in Switzerland and Japan, and fisheries in Nova Scotia and Indonesia.
In it Ostrom set out eight design principles found in long-lasting common-pool resource institutions.
It argues that self-interest need not always cause degradation and can lead people to care for common property resources.

notes: Phrase concept (a book) with no page of its own; may fold into Ostrom's design principles or the Ostrom founder entry.

title: Polycentric governance

definition.text: Polycentric governance, introduced by Vincent Ostrom, is governance through many overlapping, independent decision-making centres, argued to improve efficiency, accountability and problem-solving.

facts.text: Some question whether it works where institutions are weak or corruption is high.
In a polycentric network, a resource that cannot be monitored as a whole is less likely to be well managed, as with space debris.

contested_note: Critics question whether polycentric governance applies where institutional capacity is weak or corruption is high.
notes: Phrase concept with no page of its own.

title: Joint Forest Management

definition.text: Joint Forest Management is India's term for partnerships in which state forest departments and local communities share forest protection and development.

facts.text: It is set out in India's National Forest Policy of 1988 and guidelines of 1990, and began in Odisha in 1988.
With Nepal's Forest User Groups, it was an early response to failing centralized forest policy.
